children: Saudi Arabia’s Humain and DataVolt have expanded their partnership to develop 100 megawatts (MW) of an AI-ready data centre at Oxagon, NEOM’s industrial city on the Red Sea coast.
The 100MW facility will form part of the 360MW first phase of DataVolt’s planned 1.5 gigawatts (GW) AI data centre campus at Oxagon, Humain announced in a press statement on Monday.
Construction is underway, with the first 100MW of capacity expected to become available in 2028.

The facility is expected to integrate renewable energy sources, advanced cooling technologies and high-performance computing clusters to support large-scale AI and cloud workloads, the statement said.
Humain, a Public Investment Fund (PIF) company, is focused on developing full-stack AI capabilities, while Saudi-based DataVolt develops and operates digital infrastructure.
The announcement didn’t specify the investment value of the 100MW development and the timeline for the remaining 260MW of the first phase.

Last week, Saudi-listed Al Moammar Information Systems Company (MIS) announced that it has been awarded a contract by Humain to expand the capacity of the PIF-owned company’s data centre from 50 MW to 250 MW.
(Writing by SA Kader; Editing by Anoop Menon)

title: HUMAIN, DataVolt expand partnership for 100MW AI data centre at NEOM in Saudi Arabia
